lines.say: Five identical resistors, and the voltmeter reads one volt. What's the voltage across the battery?
This is a real question from a 2019 admissions test, and loads of people get it wrong. Pause and have a go!
First, look at where the voltmeter is. {a}It's only across one of the two bottom resistors.
Those two are identical, so they share the voltage equally. {a}One volt each, {b}so two volts across the bottom branch.
Now here's the bit people miss. {a}The top resistor is in parallel with that branch, {b}so it gets the same two volts.
Let's call each resistance R. {a}The top one carries two over R, the bottom branch carries one over R, {b}so three over R in total.
All of that current goes through {a}both outside resistors. {b}Three over R, times R, is three volts each.
So add it all the way round: {a}three, plus two, plus three. That's eight volts! {b}The answer is E.
If you picked answer A, {a}don't stress, that's the classic trap. {b}You used one volt for the whole parallel bit, instead of just one resistor.
